name: Sopater
overview: Sopater was a male believer from Berea mentioned in the book of Acts. Beyond his identification as a follower of Christ from this city, Scripture provides limited additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Sopater appears once in Acts 20:4 without a given meaning or special title. It is simply presented as his proper name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Sopater was the son of Pyrrhus, as inferred from Acts 20:4. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Sopater's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a believer from Berea, a city noted for its receptiveness to the gospel. His mention alongside other companions in Acts 20:4 highlights his participation in the early Christian mission and support of the Apostle Paul. This association underscores his commitment to the spread of the gospel during the formative years of the church.
